notes:
{物|もの} is one of the most versatile words in Japanese, referring to physical objects, abstract things, or general matters. As a noun it typically refers to tangible items, but in combination with adjectives (e.g. ⟦{甘|あま}い→甘い：00617_amai⟧{物|もの}) it means "something [adjective]."

もの VS こと:
- {物|もの}: concrete or tangible things, or abstract things treated as entities
- ⟦こと→こと：01164_koto⟧: abstract matters, facts, events, or actions
- Example: ⟦{大切|たいせつ}な→大切：01456_taisetsu⟧{物|もの} (a precious thing/item) vs ⟦{大切|たいせつ}な→大切：01456_taisetsu⟧⟦こと→こと：01164_koto⟧ (an important matter/fact)

COMPOUNDS:
- ⟦{食べ物|たべもの}→食べ物：02890_tabemono⟧: food
- ⟦{飲み物|のみもの}→飲み物：02929_nomimono⟧: drink
- ⟦{買い物|かいもの}→買い物：00853_kaimono⟧: shopping
- ⟦{着物|きもの}→着物：01309_kimono⟧: kimono, clothes
- ⟦{物語|ものがたり}→物語：03634_monogatari⟧: story, tale
- ⟦{荷物|にもつ}→荷物：00737_nimotsu⟧: luggage, baggage

COMMON PATTERNS:
もの (or もん in casual speech) also appears as a sentence-ending particle expressing explanation, reason, or mild complaint: ⟦だって→だって：03423_datte⟧⟦{高|たか}い→高い：00500_takai⟧んだもの (But it's expensive!).
